text:
mira: Heads up — ACME on a Private deployment reported an admin user couldn't access the control plane UI or list nodes after yesterday's RBAC refactor. Not customer-facing yet but blocking their ops team.
chris: Which role was affected? onprem-admin or the PCP admin shim?
mira: They were mapped to `onprem-admin` via SAML group mapping. Audit shows a 403 on GET /controlplane/nodes for user acme-admin@acme.com.
alex: Can you paste the request id / log snippet?
mira: Log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T21:14:23Z request=req_9f3a93 user=acme-admin@acme.com action=GET /controlplane/nodes auth=ok token_subject=svc-acme-deploy-svc subject_chain=[user:acme-admin, svc:svc-acme-deploy-svc] policy_eval=deny(reason=missing_group:acme-admins) effective_principal=svc-acme-deploy-svc
```
chris: Hmm. Looks like the service account is becoming the effective principal. We shipped a precedence change in the RBAC refactor that favors service-account principals if present.
leo: If that's true, audit.v1.events should show the subject chain and effective principal. Also double-check KMS-wrapped session tokens — if claim decryption failed we might be falling back to the service token path.
mira: I pulled full audit entries: subject_chain exactly as above and effective=svc-acme-deploy-svc. Ticket TF-3924 created internally.
alex: Short-term fix: treat explicit human principals as higher precedence than service tokens unless the session has an `impersonation-allowed` flag set by policy. Long-term: add a simulation suite.
chris: Agreed. For mitigation: we can either revert the precedence change on that customer's control plane or add a temporary allow rule adding `acme-admins` to their cluster RBAC. Which is less risky?
mira: Customer prefers a small allowlist change to avoid a rollback. I'll push a patch to their private config. Example patch to apply:
```
apiVersion: rbac.redwood.ai/v1
kind: RBACOverride
metadata:
  name: acme-temp-allow
spec:
  allow:
    - principal: group:acme-admins
      resources:
        - controlplane/*
      actions: ["*"]
```
kubectl apply -f rbac-override-acme.yaml --context=acme-private
```
leo: Also consider rotating the KMS key used for service tokens if there's any chance a token was over-privileged. And add an alert on `effective_principal != original_subject` for private control planes.
mira: Will open a PR to revert precedence and include unit + integration tests to cover subject_chain ordering. PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/internal/acme/rbac/merge/123
security-bot: Automated triage: classified as privilege misassignment (P2). No code-exec. Logged as SEC-2026-117.
oncall-bot: Created incident channel #incident/ACME-rbac-1812345678 and paged oncall @chris.
chris: I'll coordinate the allowlist change + smoke tests. After the PR, run `authz-sim` against ACME's audit logs and validate that human principals remain effective when present.
mira: Plan recap:
  1) apply temp allowlist for acme-admins (done by me)
  2) PR for precedence fix + tests (mira + alex)
  3) add alert + KMS key review (leo)
  4) customer postmortem and update runbook
I'll update TF-3924 with timestamps and link to incident channel.
alex: :thumbsup: I'll review the PR today and help test.
chris: After patch, we should schedule a canary rollout to a single private control plane then roll out globally.
mira: Thanks all — updating incident channel now and looping in support for the customer call.
